title: Everything becomes whole when Naam lives inside
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: The shabad begins by calling the path and cleansing bath perfect when the Name is in the heart. It keeps extending that wholeness through peace, contentment, yoga, glory, and the Creator's presence.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels living with a chronic sense of incompletion and searching for patches everywhere else. Held quietly, it teaches that wholeness grows from sanctuary and Naam, not from frantic improvement.
takeaway: Let this stay with you: wholeness begins when the Name is kept in the heart.

lines.translation: Perfect is the path; perfect is the cleansing bath.
Everything is perfect, if the Naam is in the heart. ||1||
One's honor remains perfect, when the Perfect Lord preserves it.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਕੀ ਸਰਣਿ ਜਨ ਤਾਕੀ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: paarabraham kee saran jan taakee ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: His servant takes to the Sanctuary of the Supreme Lord God. ||1||Pause||
Perfect is the peace; perfect is the contentment.
Perfect is the penance; perfect is the Raja Yoga, the Yoga of meditation and success. ||2||
On the Lord's Path, sinners are purified.
Perfect is their glory; perfect is their humanity. ||3||
They dwell forever in the Presence of the Creator Lord.
Says Nanak, my True Guru is Perfect. ||4||45||114||

structure: First, it begins by placing perfection inside the heart that holds Naam.
Then, it shows peace, contentment, honor, and humanity becoming whole under that same keeping.
Finally, it ends with the servant sheltered in the Supreme Lord and the True Guru confessed as complete.
